paper.title: Adaptive Sensor Placement for Continuous Spaces

settings.name_in_paper: Adaptive sensor placement as a continuum-armed bandit with Poisson process feedback
unmapped: Events arrive each round from an inhomogeneous Poisson process with unknown rate lambda on [0,1]; the learner observes the locations of events falling in the sensed set A_t (point-process feedback)
Actions are unions of at most U disjoint subintervals of [0,1]; expected reward r(A)=int_A (lambda(x)-C) dx with known per-unit sensing cost C
Rate function bounded by a known lambda_max; the learner knows lambda_max, the cost C and the number of sensors U
Prior over lambda (truncated Gamma histogram prior) used to define Bayesian regret
settings.definition_quote: In each of a series of rounds $t \in \mathds{N}$, $m_t \geq 0$ events of interest arise at locations $X_{t,1},...,X_{t,m_t} \in [0,1]$ according to a non-homogeneous Poisson process with rate $\lambda: [0,1] \rightarrow \mathds{R}_+$. $U$ sensors are deployed in each round with each sensor observing a distinct subinterval of $[0,1]$; the action space ${\mathcal A}$ consists of the sets of at most $U$ disjoint intervals of $[0,1]$. ... $r(A) = \int_{A}(\lambda(x)-C)\,{\rm d}x$

algorithms.name: Thompson Sampling with increasingly granular Bayesian histograms (truncated Gamma priors) and AS-IM action selection

symbols.K_up: constant overline{K} with K_t <= K_up t^{1/3}
symbols.K_low: constant underline{K} with K_t >= K_low t^{1/3}
symbols.lambda_max: known upper bound on the Poisson rate function (prior truncation point)
symbols.C_cost: cost per unit length of sensing
symbols.U: number of sensors (max number of intervals)

conditions: lambda drawn from the prior (Bayesian regret)
tuning: number of bins K_t satisfies K_low t^{1/3} <= K_t <= K_up t^{1/3}
truncated Gamma priors TG(alpha, beta, 0, lambda_max)

source.label: thm::regretupper
source.quote: Consider the setup of Section \ref{sec.model}, with $U$ sensors, and cost of sensing $C$. Suppose we choose $K_t$ such that there exist positive constants $\underline{K},\overline{K}$ such that $\underline{K}t^{1/3}\leq K_t\leq \overline{K}t^{1/3}$. Then the Bayesian regret of Algorithm \ref{alg::TS} satisfies BReg(T) \leq 4\overline{K}\big(\log(T+1)\log(T) + 2\lambda_{\max}\big)T^{1/3} + \big(CU\underline{K}^{-1} + \sqrt{24\overline{K}\lambda_{\max}\log(T)}\big)T^{2/3}.

results.notes: Comparator is the optimal continuous action A* (union of <= U intervals). Bound is O(T^{2/3} sqrt(log T)). Feedback mapped to semi_bandit (event locations observed within the sensed region); setting mapping to continuum_other is approximate. Algorithm schedule does not depend on T so recorded anytime. Theorem 1 (AS-IM computational optimality, O(K_t log K_t)) is not a regret guarantee and is not recorded.
